The journey began by learning the AWS account, billing and console boundaries before creating infrastructure that could quietly become a bill.

Architecture / mental model

AWS account → Management Console / CLI → Region → service → resource
             ↘ Billing & Cost Management / Free Tier tracking

How it works

The AWS Management Console is the browser interface into AWS services, but the account and Region context matter before any resource is created. Many resources are regional, while identity and billing concepts have broader account scope.

AWS Free Tier is a billing program, not a magic sandbox. AWS changed the new-customer model in July 2025: new customers can choose a Free or Paid account plan, receive initial credits and may earn additional credits, while Always Free offers still have service-specific monthly limits.

The first operational habit is therefore cost visibility. Check the current Free Tier/credit state and Billing dashboard before experiments, and know which Region you are using so a forgotten resource does not survive somewhere you stopped looking.

Hands-on reference

aws sts get-caller-identity
aws configure list
aws ec2 describe-regions --query 'Regions[].RegionName' --output table

Verification

Confirm the account identity, active Region and Free Tier/credit information in Billing. Create nothing until you can explain where AWS would show its cost and where you would delete it.

Field note / gotcha

Free Tier eligibility depends on account age/plan and service-specific limits. A service being 'Free Tier eligible' does not mean every configuration of that service is free.

Security considerations

Protect the root user, enable MFA, create administrative identities for routine work instead of using root, and keep billing alerts/visibility available to the people responsible for the account.

What I learned

Cloud engineering starts with account, identity, Region and cost awareness. The fastest infrastructure to delete is the one you never accidentally created.
